{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, the passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same story.","text":"It sounded like her brother. Mara kept walking.

Behind her, the porch steps groaned. “Mara, wait.”

She had buried Daniel in February. She had stood beside his grave while rain filled the print of her shoes. Whatever had called her name could explain itself from a distance.

The quarry path narrowed between blackberry canes. Mara stopped where the trees opened onto the water and turned. A woman stood beneath the branches, one hand pressed to her side. She wore Daniel’s old green coat.

“Who are you?” Mara asked.

“His wife,” the woman said. “I’m Lena.”

Daniel had never mentioned a wife. Then again, for the last six years, he had mentioned very little.

“Why did you call me like that?”

“He taught me.” Lena swallowed. “He thought you might run.”

Mara looked past her toward the dark house. “What boat?”

“There wasn’t one. He said you’d know the note was wrong, and you wouldn’t knock.” Lena took a careful step forward. “There’s a man waiting inside. He came this morning with a key and said Daniel owed him something.”

The water below them gave a soft, hollow knock against the quarry wall. Mara remembered the bicycle sinking there, its red handlebars the last thing to disappear.

“What did Daniel owe?”

Lena opened her coat. Beneath it, strapped against her ribs, was a small metal box.

“I don’t know,” she said. “But he left this for you. And the man inside knew about it.”

From the house came the sudden slam of a door. Lena flinched. Mara held out her hand."}
